sources.title: Exact repository interview question and Batch 0033 frozen source boundary
Mode-set median deterministic JDK 21 validation against independent TreeMap oracle

claims.text: The source asks for array mode(s) and the median among their values; tie, even-median, invalid-input and API semantics are answer-side contracts.
The exact fenced Java implementation counts frequencies, retains all maximum-frequency values, sorts them, and computes the declared median with overflow-safe even-case arithmetic.
The JDK 21 fixture passes named edge cases, invalid inputs and all 9,840 bounded arrays against an independent TreeMap oracle.

boundary_tests.expected: all arrays length 1..8 over {-1,0,1} match independent TreeMap oracle

findings: The preserved repository source asks only for the mode(s) of a given array and the median among the mode values; type, tied-mode API, even-cardinality median semantics, null/empty behavior, mutation policy and implementation language are not preserved.

The candidate keeps those missing details explicit as answer-side contracts: int input, all maximum-frequency distinct values as the mode set, arithmetic-mean median for an even mode count, null/empty rejection, non-mutation and a Java Result API.

The displayed Java implementation is byte-for-byte identical to the validated ModeMedian.java fixture and compiles under JDK 21; sorting the collected modes removes any dependency on HashMap iteration order.
Casting before the even-median addition makes the Integer.MIN_VALUE/Integer.MAX_VALUE boundary overflow-safe and the fixed test verifies -0.5.
The TreeMap oracle checks all 9,840 non-empty arrays of lengths 1..8 over {-1,0,1}, in addition to named single-mode, tied-mode, signed, extreme-integer and all-distinct cases plus invalid inputs.

The answer covers complexity, state definition, input/output contract, edge cases, a selection-algorithm variant, and topic-specific follow-ups without fabricated project experience or unrelated content.
